description: Who holds a Georgia wrongful death claim when a child dies, what a jury decides about the full value of the child's life, and the deadlines that apply.
shortAnswer: If the child did not leave a spouse or a child of his own, the wrongful death claim belongs to the parents. The jury is not asked to put a price on the parents’ grief. The jury is asked to decide the full value of the child’s life, measured from the point of view of the child.

sections.heading: The claim belongs to the parents
sections.shortAnswer: In every case of the homicide of a child, there shall be some party entitled to recover the full value of the life of the child. If the child did not leave a spouse or a child of his own, the claim belongs to the parents.

sections.heading: It does not matter how old your child was
sections.shortAnswer: Section 19-7-1(c) applies to the death of a child “minor or sui juris.” If your 19-year-old son was killed in a wreck, and he was not married and had no children, the wrongful death claim is yours.

sections.heading: When the parents are not together
sections.shortAnswer: Divorce does not end either parent’s right. If one parent refuses to proceed, or cannot be located, the other parent may bring the claim for both. Either parent may file a motion before trial asking the judge to apportion the recovery fairly.

sections.heading: What “the full value of the life” means
sections.shortAnswer: The economic part is what the child would have earned and contributed over a lifetime. The intangible part is the value of living the life itself. It is left to the enlightened conscience of the jury.

sections.heading: The estate has a separate claim
sections.shortAnswer: Under O.C.G.A. § 51-4-5(b), the administrator of the child’s estate may recover the funeral, medical, and other necessary expenses resulting from the injury and death.

sections.heading: Unborn children
sections.shortAnswer: For an unborn child, the right to recover the full value of the life begins once a detectable human heartbeat is present. That is much earlier in a pregnancy than quickening.

sections.heading: The deadline does not wait for grief
sections.shortAnswer: The wrongful death claim must generally be filed within two years of the child’s death. A parent’s wrongful death claim belongs to the parent, and it runs from the date of death.

sections.heading: What I tell grieving parents
sections.shortAnswer: Do not talk to the other side’s insurance company about how your child died. Preserve the evidence. Talk to a lawyer before you sign anything, including a release from an insurance company.

faq.q: Can divorced parents both sue for the wrongful death of their child in Georgia?
faq.a: Yes. If the parents are divorced, separated, or living apart, the claim belongs to both of them. The recovery is divided equally between the parents, unless a judge is asked to divide it differently.

faq.q: Can parents sue for the wrongful death of an adult child in Georgia?
faq.a: Section 19-7-1(c) applies to the death of a child “minor or sui juris.” If your 19-year-old son was killed in a wreck, and he was not married and had no children, the wrongful death claim is yours, just as it would have been when he was 9.

faq.q: How is the value of a child's life calculated in a Georgia wrongful death case?
faq.a: A child has no paycheck yet. That does not make the economic part zero. Economists project it from the child’s likely education, the family’s background, and the working life the child probably would have had. The intangible part is often the larger part of a child’s case.

faq.q: Does the minor tolling statute extend the deadline for a child's wrongful death claim?
faq.a: No. That statute protects a child’s own claim while the child is a child. A parent’s wrongful death claim belongs to the parent, and it runs from the date of death.
